findings.issue_text: Duplicate `def self.downsize` in `app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-151`: Ruby has no method overloading, so the second 3-arg definition at line 149 silently discards the width/height definition at line 145, breaking every existing 4-arg/5-arg caller (the `OptimizedImage.create_for` thumbnail path and specs) with `ArgumentError (5 for 3..4)` or `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` — avatar and post thumbnail generation breaks site-wide

In-place ImageMagick convert at `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67`: `downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` writes the output over its own input, which is unsupported IM usage; for large images the source can be truncated or overwritten while still being decoded, and a mid-write failure (e.g., ENOSPC on the temp fs) permanently destroys the upload bytes before `Upload.create_for` runs, leaving the original unrecoverable and producing a misleading downstream error

Downsize result ignored in the shrink loop at `uploads_controller.rb:66-69`: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns true/false but the loop never checks it, so if convert fails every iteration the real failure is masked and the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` as if nothing happened; additionally, 80% scaling per attempt converges to ~32.8% linearly / ~10.7% in bytes, so inputs more than ~9× the limit (reachable via direct API uploads) exit the loop still oversized and are passed on — broken error propagation

Hardcoded 10MB replaces site settings on both client checks and the server URL-download cap (`utilities.js:182`, `utilities.js:246`, `uploads_controller.rb:55`): `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` are no longer consulted client-side and the API URL download cap moved to a fixed `10.megabytes`; sites with limits above 10MB can no longer upload valid files (API URL downloads >10MB return nil, causing a 422 'undefined method size for nil'), sites with limits below 10MB show users a wrong 'maximum size is 10240 KB' message on 413, and attachments — never downsized server-side — pass the client gate up to 10MB only to be rejected by the server

Animated GIFs are corrupted because the `.GIF$` extension check in `optimize` (`from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) can never match this call site: `from` is an extension-less tempfile path (RackMultipart or `discourse-upload-<type>`), so the `allow_animation` branch (`downsize_instructions_animated` with `-coalesce`) is unreachable regardless of the setting, and large animated GIFs are resized without coalesce — the classic IM failure producing misaligned/composited broken frames

Corrupt-output verification in `convert_with` is skipped at this call site: the destination tempfile has no image extension, so the verification gated on `FileHelper.is_image?(to)` never runs and the broken GIF output passes as success

`allow_animated_thumbnails` is the wrong setting to gate whether a user's upload keeps animation: it governs whether thumbnails animate, so admins who disabled animated thumbnails would silently flatten users' oversized animated GIF avatars/uploads even once the extension bug is fixed

The shrink guard at `uploads_controller.rb:64` ignores upload `type`: `create_upload` handles both image and attachment types, but the guard uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` plus `max_image_size_kb` unconditionally, so a within-limit image attachment (e.g., a 6MB PNG with max_attachment_size_kb=15MB / max_image_size_kb=4MB) is silently recompressed and shrunk — the stored 'original' is not what the user uploaded — while with a smaller attachment limit it is pointlessly processed and then still rejected

Duplicate `downsize` definition in `app/models/optimized_image.rb` shadows the 4-arg version with a new 3-arg signature (Ruby keeps the last definition), so every existing call site passing width and height separately breaks — `height` lands in `opts` and `optimize` evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer causing a TypeError (5-arg calls raise ArgumentError), hard-crashing the thumbnail/avatar pipeline

Up to 5 blind, sequential, full-image re-encodes run synchronously in the upload request thread (`uploads_controller.rb:63-70`): each pass is a complete ImageMagick decode+encode via a blocking shell-out, and the fixed 20%-per-pass schedule converges slowly, so files far over `max_image_size_kb` (now common with the raised 10MB client cap) burn all 5 passes, costing seconds of CPU and added latency per upload while blocking a web worker — a single adaptive scale would achieve the same result for ~1/5 the work

The downsizing loop never verifies success: `convert_with`'s `false` return is ignored and there is no post-loop size check, so on convert failure the loop runs 5 futile full passes on an unchanged or truncated in-place tempfile, then unconditionally hands it to `Upload.create_for` — wasting all encode work and letting the user hit a generic too-large rejection or a half-written/corrupt file proceed to upload; should `break` on convert failure and assert `tempfile.size <= SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` before `create_for`

Hardcoded 10MB replaces SiteSetting-driven limits in three places (`utilities.js:181`, `utilities.js:246`, `uploads_controller.rb:55`): sites with limits below 10MB let users pass client validation and transfer the full file only to be rejected server-side (pure waste for attachments since the downsizing loop is image-only), sites with limits above 10MB wrongly block valid images client-side, the 413 message claims "10240 KB" regardless of the real enforced limit, and if the reverse-proxy body-size limit still derives from old settings, oversized requests 413 before the new loop can ever run

Unvalidated images run through convert up to 5 times with no ImageMagick resource limits (`-limit`/policy/timeout) and no pixel-dimension validation before the loop, so a small-but-huge-dimension decompression-bomb image forces massive per-pass allocations multiplied by up to 5 passes on attacker-controlled input, letting a cheap client request consume gigabytes of memory/disk-cache

Animated-GIF branch is effectively unreachable for this flow: the `_animated` instructions in `optimize` (`optimized_image.rb:~155`) are selected only when the tempfile path ends in `.gif`, but composer uploads are Rack multipart tempfiles and API downloads are named `discourse-upload-<type>…` with no `.gif` extension — so `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` never takes effect at the new call site, large animated GIFs go through the plain non-coalescing pipeline up to 5 times (risking mangled frame-optimized output with no size reduction), and a thumbnail setting is silently repurposed to govern original uploads

Duplicate `def self.downsize` definitions in app/models/optimized_image.rb — Ruby has no method overloading, so the second definition silently replaces the first for all call sites; existing callers passing width/height positionally (e.g., OptimizedImage.create_for thumbnail generation) now bind the height Integer to `opts`, causing NoMethodError (undefined method '[]' for Integer) on 4-arg calls and ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments 5 for 3..4) on 5-arg calls, breaking all optimized-image/thumbnail generation

Downsizing retry loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-70 ignores the `false` return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (returned when ImageMagick exits non-zero), has no rescue around the backtick (Errno::ENOENT if binary missing), and convert_with sends stderr to /dev/null — deterministic failures are fully silent, the loop blindly retries 5 times, then falls through to Upload.create_for with a still-oversized or truncated tempfile

Heavy, unbounded image processing moved into the synchronous request path — up to 5 sequential ImageMagick conversions run per upload request in the request thread via shell backtick with no timeout, and there is no server-side size ceiling before conversion (the 10MB cap exists only in client JS and is bypassable via API/direct POST), creating a worker-starvation/DoS vector and multi-second latency; should be a background job or have a hard pre-conversion size cap and per-invocation timeout

Hardcoded 10 * 1024 / 10.megabytes replaces SiteSettings lookups in three places (utilities.js:182, utilities.js:246, uploads_controller.rb:55) — client-side precheck, server 413 messages, and FileHelper.download cap no longer honor max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb, so attachments above 10MB are blocked client-side, sites with limits above 10MB can't upload accepted images, and users see wrong 'max 10MB' error text for files under 10MB

Animated-GIF branch in optimize (from =~ /\.GIF$/i) is unreachable for browser uploads because it detects GIFs via the tempfile path extension, which Rack multipart tempfiles lack — animated GIFs always take the non-animated instructions (no -coalesce), potentially mangling optimized/delta-frame GIFs even when allow_animation: true is passed
allow_animated_thumbnails, a thumbnail policy setting, is misused as the gate for deciding animation handling of the full-size stored upload

In-place convert (from == to: downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)) makes ImageMagick write output over its own input — a failure mid-write (disk full, crash) truncates/corrupts the only copy of the upload, and the corrupt file is then fed to Upload.create_for; should use a temp output path plus move

The 5 × 80% downsizing budget cannot reach small site maxima — each pass scales to 80% (~64% of file size per iteration, only ~10.7% after 5 passes), so on sites with max_image_size_kb well below 1/10th of the uploaded size (e.g., 512KB max with a 9.9MB image) the loop exhausts all 5 heavy IM runs and the upload is still rejected, with no early error and no stronger fallback resize

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication.rationale: The new upload resizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, passing the same path for both input (`from`) and output (`to`). Writing output over the input file during an external conversion can corrupt/truncate the source on failure (e.g., disk full) before `Upload.create_for` runs, causing irreversible data loss and confusing downstream errors.

adjudication.rationale: In the new upload downsizing loop (uploads_controller.rb), animated handling relies on `OptimizedImage.optimize` detecting GIFs via `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The call site passes `from` as `tempfile.path` (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`). For the URL-download branch, the tempfile is created via `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`, which provides a prefix without an extension, making it plausible/likely that `tempfile.path` does not end with `.gif`. In that case the `_animated` instructions (with `-coalesce`) are not used even when `allow_animation` is true, so animated GIFs can be processed with non-animated instructions, which is known to corrupt/miscompose frames. The diff shows this new resizing behavior and the extension-based check, so the defect is exposed/introduced here.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedImage.convert_with` only executes the conversion command and checks `$?.exitstatus`; there is no corrupt-output verification and no gating on `FileHelper.is_image?(to)` anywhere in the shown changes. The finding references behavior (“verification gated on `FileHelper.is_image?(to)`”) that is not present in this diff, so it can’t be verified against the provided code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `allow_animated_thumbnails` is the wrong setting to gate whether a user's upload keeps animation: it governs whether thumbnails animate, so admins who disabled animated thumbnails would silently flatten users' oversized animated GIF avatars/uploads even once the extension bug is fixed

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, oversized images are repeatedly downsized via `OptimizedImage.downsize(... allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, `allow_animation` controls whether the `_animated` instruction path is used for `.GIF` inputs; if false, it will use the non-animated instructions, which can flatten/strip animation during downsizing. Since this downsizing is applied to the user’s actual uploaded file (not just thumbnails), tying animation preservation to `allow_animated_thumbnails` can cause unintended loss of animation for oversized GIF uploads when that setting is disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The shrink guard at `uploads_controller.rb:64` ignores upload `type`: `create_upload` handles both image and attachment types, but the guard uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` plus `max_image_size_kb` unconditionally, so a within-limit image attachment (e.g., a 6MB PNG with max_attachment_size_kb=15MB / max_image_size_kb=4MB) is silently recompressed and shrunk — the stored 'original' is not what the user uploaded — while with a smaller attachment limit it is pointlessly processed and then still rejected

adjudication.rationale: The new shrink loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` runs for any upload whose `filename` looks like an image (`FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`) and uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` as the threshold, without considering the `type` argument (which `create_upload(type, ...)` receives). This means an image uploaded under a non-image type (e.g. attachment) can be recompressed/downscaled to the image limit even if `max_attachment_size_kb` would allow the original, changing what is stored as the “original” upload. Conversely, if attachment limits are lower than `max_image_size_kb`, the shrink may still occur (when over `max_image_size_kb`) but the result can still exceed the attachment limit and be rejected, making the processing potentially wasted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate `downsize` definition in `app/models/optimized_image.rb` shadows the 4-arg version with a new 3-arg signature (Ruby keeps the last definition), so every existing call site passing width and height separately breaks — `height` lands in `opts` and `optimize` evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer causing a TypeError (5-arg calls raise ArgumentError), hard-crashing the thumbnail/avatar pipeline

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a second `self.downsize` definition in `app/models/optimized_image.rb` with a different signature (`def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`) after an earlier 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. In Ruby the later method overwrites the earlier one, so existing call sites that pass `max_width, max_height` will bind `opts` to an Integer (`max_height`). Then `optimize` does `opts[:allow_animation]`, which will raise a TypeError when `opts` is an Integer. This is a real, diff-grounded breaking change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds synchronous image downsizing inside the upload request path: in `uploads_controller.rb` it loops up to 5 times while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` each iteration. `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately shells out via backticks in `convert_with`, so each iteration is a blocking ImageMagick decode/encode. This is a concrete perf/latency concern introduced by the change (not a correctness bug), and the fixed repeated passes (`attempt = 5` with `"80%"`) can indeed trigger multiple full re-encodes for large images.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The downsizing loop never verifies success: `convert_with`'s `false` return is ignored and there is no post-loop size check, so on convert failure the loop runs 5 futile full passes on an unchanged or truncated in-place tempfile, then unconditionally hands it to `Upload.create_for` — wasting all encode work and letting the user hit a generic too-large rejection or a half-written/corrupt file proceed to upload; should `break` on convert failure and assert `tempfile.size <= SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` before `create_for`

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` but ignores its success/failure return; `OptimizedImage.convert_with` explicitly returns `false` on non-zero exit status. The loop condition only re-checks `tempfile.size`, so a failed convert can cause up to 5 repeated attempts with no progress, and the code then unconditionally calls `Upload.create_for(...)` without asserting `tempfile.size <= SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, potentially proceeding with an unchanged too-large file or a partially-written in-place output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded 10MB replaces SiteSetting-driven limits in three places (`utilities.js:181`, `utilities.js:246`, `uploads_controller.rb:55`): sites with limits below 10MB let users pass client validation and transfer the full file only to be rejected server-side (pure waste for attachments since the downsizing loop is image-only), sites with limits above 10MB wrongly block valid images client-side, the 413 message claims "10240 KB" regardless of the real enforced limit, and if the reverse-proxy body-size limit still derives from old settings, oversized requests 413 before the new loop can ever run

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly replaces SiteSetting-driven max size checks with a hardcoded 10MB in two client-side paths (`utilities.js` file size check and 413 handler) and in the server-side URL download limit (`uploads_controller.rb` uses `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`). This makes configured limits ineffective: sites with limits >10MB will be blocked client-side at 10MB, and sites with limits <10MB will have client-side messaging/validation out of sync with the real server limit (the 413 alert will always show 10240KB). The new downsizing loop is image-only, so it doesn’t address oversized non-image uploads passing a mismatched client check.

This creates a plausible DoS vector (e.g., large-dimension/decompression-bomb images) amplified by up to 5 passes.

adjudication.rationale: In the new upload downsizing loop (`uploads_controller.rb`), the call is `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. In `optimized_image.rb`, the animated branch is chosen only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, i.e., based on the *tempfile path* extension. The diff also shows API downloads use `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`, which provides a basename without `.gif`, and multipart tempfiles commonly have no `.gif` suffix. Since the code passes `tempfile.path` (not the original filename), `_animated` instructions will often never be selected, so `allow_animation` won’t take effect for animated GIF uploads in this flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsizing retry loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-70 ignores the `false` return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (returned when ImageMagick exits non-zero), has no rescue around the backtick (Errno::ENOENT if binary missing), and convert_with sends stderr to /dev/null — deterministic failures are fully silent, the loop blindly retries 5 times, then falls through to Upload.create_for with a still-oversized or truncated tempfile

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times but never checks its return value, even though `OptimizedImage.convert_with` returns `false` when the ImageMagick command exits non-zero (`return false if $?.exitstatus != 0`). Also, `convert_with` redirects output to `/dev/null` via backticks (`` `#{...} &> /dev/null` ``), so failures are silent and the loop will blindly retry and then proceed to `Upload.create_for` even if downsizing never succeeded. However, the finding’s claim about needing a `rescue` for `Errno::ENOENT` from the backtick is not clearly supported by the diff alone, since backticks invoke a shell and typically won’t raise that exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Heavy, unbounded image processing moved into the synchronous request path — up to 5 sequential ImageMagick conversions run per upload request in the request thread via shell backtick with no timeout, and there is no server-side size ceiling before conversion (the 10MB cap exists only in client JS and is bypassable via API/direct POST), creating a worker-starvation/DoS vector and multi-second latency; should be a background job or have a hard pre-conversion size cap and per-invocation timeout

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds synchronous, potentially expensive image processing in the upload request path: in `uploads_controller.rb` it loops up to 5 times calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes ImageMagick via shell backticks with no timeout (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null` ``), so each request can block a Rails worker for multiple conversions. There is also no hard pre-conversion upper bound for normal multipart uploads in this new code (it will attempt to downsize any oversized image), and the 10MB limit shown in the diff is only enforced client-side (JS) and for API URL downloads (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`), not for direct POST uploads. This creates a realistic DoS/latency risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded 10 * 1024 / 10.megabytes replaces SiteSettings lookups in three places (utilities.js:182, utilities.js:246, uploads_controller.rb:55) — client-side precheck, server 413 messages, and FileHelper.download cap no longer honor max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb, so attachments above 10MB are blocked client-side, sites with limits above 10MB can't upload accepted images, and users see wrong 'max 10MB' error text for files under 10MB

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes a 10MB limit in three places that previously depended on site settings: utilities.js changes `maxSizeKB` from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to `10 * 1024`, the 413 handler changes from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to `10 * 1024`, and uploads_controller.rb changes FileHelper.download’s cap from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes`. This removes configurability and can block uploads/downloads when the site setting is >10MB (client-side precheck and URL download), and it can display incorrect “max 10MB” messaging when the configured limit differs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated-GIF branch in optimize (from =~ /\.GIF$/i) is unreachable for browser uploads because it detects GIFs via the tempfile path extension, which Rack multipart tempfiles lack — animated GIFs always take the non-animated instructions (no -coalesce), potentially mangling optimized/delta-frame GIFs even when allow_animation: true is passed

adjudication.rationale: The new upload-reduction loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` in `UploadsController#create_upload`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated-GIF path is selected only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, i.e. based on the *tempfile path* extension. Since `from` here is a Rack multipart tempfile path (not the original `filename`), the animated branch can fail to trigger for uploaded GIFs even when `allow_animation: true` is passed, causing non-animated instructions to be used during downsizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: allow_animated_thumbnails, a thumbnail policy setting, is misused as the gate for deciding animation handling of the full-size stored upload

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new auto-downsize loop for oversized images calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `optimized_image.rb`, `allow_animation` directly controls whether GIFs use `*_instructions_animated` (i.e., whether animation is preserved/handled) for this full-size upload processing. The diff shows a thumbnail-specific setting (`allow_animated_thumbnails`) being used to decide animation handling during upload resizing, which is a policy/semantics mismatch concern even if it may be intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place convert (from == to: downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)) makes ImageMagick write output over its own input — a failure mid-write (disk full, crash) truncates/corrupts the only copy of the upload, and the corrupt file is then fed to Upload.create_for; should use a temp output path plus move

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` downsizes images in-place: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` inside a loop. In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` delegates to `optimize`, which builds ImageMagick conversion instructions and executes them via backticks in `convert_with`, writing to the `to` path. With `from == to`, this means the conversion writes over the only copy of the tempfile; if the conversion fails mid-write (e.g., crash, disk full), the tempfile can be left truncated/corrupt and is then passed to `Upload.create_for(...)`. Using a separate output path and atomic move would avoid this corruption risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 5 × 80% downsizing budget cannot reach small site maxima — each pass scales to 80% (~64% of file size per iteration, only ~10.7% after 5 passes), so on sites with max_image_size_kb well below 1/10th of the uploaded size (e.g., 512KB max with a 9.9MB image) the loop exhausts all 5 heavy IM runs and the upload is still rejected, with no early error and no stronger fallback resize

adjudication.rationale: The new uploads_controller.rb loop tries at most 5 iterations of `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%")` while `tempfile.size` exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. Because the shrink factor and iteration count are fixed, the diff does not guarantee the image will be reduced below the site max for very large uploads / very small maxima; after 5 runs it may still be oversized and `Upload.create_for(...)` would then fail as before. This is a real edge-case/inefficiency/behavioral limitation introduced by the change (no adaptive resize or explicit failure after exhausting attempts), though the exact size-reduction per pass isn’t provable from the diff alone.
